question: A 56-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of pain and swelling in his left leg. He has a history of pancreatic cancer and is currently receiving chemotherapy. Three weeks ago, he had a similar episode in his right arm that resolved without treatment. His temperature is 38.2°C (100.8°F). Palpation of the left leg shows a tender, cord-shaped structure medial to the medial condyle of the femur. The overlying skin is erythematous. Which of the following vessels is most likely affected?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "56-year-old man with leg pain and swelling" -> "history of pancreatic cancer and chemotherapy" -> "possible thrombotic event due to cancer and treatment" -> "tender, cord-shaped structure suggests thrombosis" -> "erythema indicates inflammation" -> "most likely affected vessel is a vein" -> "great saphenous vein commonly involved in thrombosis" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with left leg swelling and pain" -> "previous episode in right arm suggests recurrent issue" -> "fever indicates possible infection or inflammation" -> "palpation reveals cord-like structure" -> "cord-like structure suggests thrombosis" -> "external iliac vein is less likely due to location" -> "deep femoral vein is a common site for DVT" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Patient has leg swelling and erythema" -> "history of cancer increases risk of venous thromboembolism" -> "cord-like structure indicates thrombosis" -> "superficial veins are often involved in thrombosis" -> "great saphenous vein is a superficial vein" -> "most likely affected vessel is great saphenous vein" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Leg pain and swelling in a cancer patient" -> "possible deep vein thrombosis (DVT)" -> "tenderness and erythema suggest inflammation" -> "deep femoral vein is a common site for DVT" -> "external iliac vein is less likely due to symptoms" -> "great saphenous vein is also a possibility" -> "unclear which vein is affected" -> 70%
analysis: The patient's presentation is consistent with superficial thrombophlebitis, likely involving the great saphenous vein, given the tender, cord-like structure and erythema in the leg. The history of cancer and recent chemotherapy increases the risk of venous thromboembolism, which can lead to superficial vein thrombosis. The great saphenous vein runs along the medial aspect of the leg, correlating with the location of the symptoms.
